details: CONFIRMED by reading the runner. The installed Claude Code 2.1.314 eval child builder pushes
no project or local settings source is added. docs/benchmark.md:110 and evals/plugin/system_rules.py:5 already record
the same fact for CLAUDE.md ("The runner sets CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1 and --setting-sources user").
So the new .claude/settings.json is inert in every paid run: the queue item's pass case "the rule file is not readable by
the agent" is not met, and the scaffold comment ("deny rules bind its Read/Grep/Glob tools") states something false for
this harness. The case behaves exactly as before the change; only the existing read-graders stand between a self-read
The runner does build --disallowed-tools from per-case data (the case's `disallowed_tools` frontmatter field exists in the
binary, and the runner itself passes path-scoped rules like Read(<dir>/**) there), so a per-case deny is likely the
route; whether `disallowed_tools` accepts a path-scoped `Read(...)` rule is not verified (PLAUSIBLE for the fix).
Size: 30 agent minutes (find the honoured channel, move the rules there, a free check of the child arguments, test).
evidence: $ LC_ALL=C grep -a -F -c -- '"--setting-sources"' <binary>   -> one eval call site with "user"
docs/benchmark.md:110: The runner sets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS=1` and `--setting-sources user`, so a
`CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` a scaffold writes never loads.
$ grep -ln settings.json evals/plugin/*/scaffold.sh  -> only critic-role-rule (no case has shown this channel works)
failing_case: Paid run of critic-role-rule under Claude Code 2.1.314. The scaffold writes .claude/settings.json with
{"permissions":{"deny":["Read(./.claude/kit/**)",...]}}. The eval runner starts the child as
`claude -p ... --permission-mode dontAsk --setting-sources user ...`, so project settings are not a source: the deny list
is never read. The critic (or the outer session) calls Read on <cwd>/.claude/kit/judge.md and gets the rule text.
Now: the read succeeds (the run is only caught afterwards by the rule-file-read-by-read grader, as before this change).
Should: the read is refused by the harness, so the rule can reach the agent only through relay's SubagentStart hook.
fix_hint: Move the deny out of the project settings file into a channel the runner honours: the case's frontmatter
`disallowed_tools` (prompt.md), e.g. Read/Grep/Glob rules scoped to **/.claude/kit/**, after a free check that the runner
copies those into the child's --disallowed-tools (and that a path-scoped rule there does not withhold Read entirely,
which the critic needs). Drop .claude/settings.json from the scaffold and fix its comment. If the runner offers no
path-scoped channel, say so in a Gap line: the read-graders are then the only guard and the owner decides.
pass_cases: 1. Paid run (or a free probe of the runner's child arguments): a Read of .claude/kit/judge.md by the outer session or by
delegate:critic is refused; the tool result is a permission denial, not the file text.
2. A Grep with path .claude/kit or pattern ROLE-RULE is refused the same way.
3. The SubagentStart hook still delivers the file: inject_addition.py for agent_type delegate:critic in the scaffolded
directory emits additionalContext containing "Project rule ROLE-RULE" (tests/test_hook_inject_addition.py style).
4. The critic can still Read src/shelf.ts and src/shelf.test.ts (the deny is limited to the rule file / .claude).
5. The scaffold still leaves `git status --porcelain` empty on master and the rule file only in master's history.
reason: prompt.md:6 holds disallowed_tools with Read(./.claude/kit/**); settings.json dropped from scaffold.sh; test asserts it. Runner honouring is unverified without a paid run.
findings.summary: the deny rules go into the fixture's .claude/settings.json, which `claude plugin eval` never loads (it starts the child with --setting-sources user), so the agent can still Read the rule file

details: CONFIRMED by reading: the assertions are assertIn("Read(./.claude/kit/**)", deny) on the scaffold's own file. That
checks the mechanism's text, not its effect; the judge base names "a test that passes with the behaviour disabled". The
queue rule asks for each new test to fail without the fix; this one fails without the settings file, but the settings
file is not the fix that works (F1). Size: 10 agent minutes, done together with F1.

deny has no effect on any paid run. The test passes with the behaviour absent; it would keep passing after a Claude Code
update that changes how settings load, or if the file were never read at all.
Should: the test fails when the deny does not reach the eval child.
fix_hint: Rewrite the test to read the channel chosen in F1 (the case's frontmatter) and assert the rule-file deny there; keep the
pass_cases: 1. With the deny moved to the runner-honoured channel (F1 fix), the test asserts the case's own frontmatter
(prompt.md `disallowed_tools`, or whatever channel is chosen) holds a rule covering .claude/kit/judge.md; removing
that rule makes the test fail.
2. The test still asserts .claude/kit/judge.md exists after the scaffold (the hook needs it) and git status is clean.
3. The test does not accept a deny that lives only in .claude/settings.json (the channel the runner ignores).
